- Median: 893 ms. Slowest attempt: 14,850 ms.

- The data records latency only for the first attempt of each payment, so retries that B handled as the second acquirer (cascade) are not included.

questions.question: Why did the approval rate for debit cards in Colombia drop on 13 August 2026?
questions.answer:
**What happened**
The drop was a routing incident, not a whole-day event. At 14:00 on 13 Aug (Bogota time) routing v14 sent 100% of CO domestic debit to Acquirer B instead of A; it was rolled back at 12:10 on 14 Aug. B approved much less, and its decline map also stopped retries on code 05 (Do not honor). Window used: 13 Aug 14:00 to 14 Aug 12:10, CO domestic debit, final approval rate (approved on first attempt or after cascade, over payments sent), against the previous 14 days. Before 14:00 on 13 Aug all CO debit traffic was on A, so the calendar day alone (79.4%, -7.14 pp vs baseline) understates the incident.

**Impact (1,004 payments in the window)**
- Final approval rate 75.6% vs 86.5% baseline: -10.95 pp. First-attempt rate 70.7% vs 84.6%.
- 759 approvals vs 869 expected at baseline: 110 approvals lost.
- USD 6,354.20 of approved volume lost (USD 47,095.86 approved of USD 61,689.16 attempted). Fees paid in the window: USD 1,186.03.

**Cause**
1. Routing v14 (CHG-0813, 13 Aug 14:00, 'cost optimization, -40 bps'). B took all 1,004 payments, and B / routing v14 explains the full -10.95 pp in the driver analysis. Issuers, card brands, 3DS states and merchant segments all fell together, so this is not issuer-specific.
2. B's decline map v2.3 (CHG-0806, 6 Aug 08:00). Its description says only 'adds R65 handling', but code 05 also became non-retryable: B's cascade rate for 05 went from a 100% baseline to 5% on 6 Aug and to 0% on every day from 7 to 14 Aug (cascade alerts, CO all card types). It did not touch CO debit earlier because B received none of it on 1 to 12 Aug. The 15 Aug hotfix CHG-0815 ('Mapping hotfix v2.3.1: R05 reclassified as soft and retryable') corroborates this.

So the loss has two layers: B declines more at first attempt, and the retry that would have recovered part of those declines was off for code 05. This is acquirer/routing-side, the kind a cascade can normally recover; here the map told it not to.

**Evidence**
- Cut-over: at 13:00 on 13 Aug all 77 payments went to A (final 85.7%); at 14:00 all 56 went to B (final 73.2%).
- 13 Aug (A before 14:00, B after): B 647 payments, first attempt 69.9%, final 74.3%; A 503 payments, first attempt 82.5%, final 85.9%. 14 Aug: B 357 payments, final 77.9%; A 850 payments, final 87.4%.
- Declines that grew (B in the window vs A's 14-day baseline, % of payments): code 05 Do not honor 13.7% vs 4.1% (137 declines); code 1A 3DS required 5.2% vs 1.1%. Insufficient funds (51) is not higher: 3.8% vs 4.2%.
- Retries (13 Aug, CO debit): B code 05 is mapped hard, 93 declines, 0% retried. On A (14-day baseline) 05 is mapped soft, 98.4% retried and 21.3% of retries approved. B retried 1A, 96 and 91 at 100%, so 05 is the only code where B's retry behaviour differs from A's.
- After the rollback: 15 Aug final approval 85.3% (all on A), inside the 1 to 12 Aug daily range of 84.8% to 88.6%.
- CO change log, 3 to 29 Aug: only CHG-0806, CHG-0813, CHG-0814 (rollback, INC-0814) and CHG-0815. No release, risk-rule, onboarding or partner notice in that period.

**Not checked / limits**
- Why B returns more 05 and 1A declines on this traffic: the data does not say; that needs B.
- The funnel before the acquirer (risk blocks, 3DS abandonment) was not examined.
- The hotfix is unproven on debit: no CO cascade alert fired from 15 to 29 Aug, but I did not check B code 05 after the hotfix, and B received no CO domestic debit in that period.

**Recommended actions**
1. Keep routing v13 (A first for CO debit); the rollback restored the rate.
2. Before moving debit to B again: confirm B's code 05 retry rate after v2.3.1 matches A's, get B to explain its 05 and 1A decline rates, and start with a small share with a guardrail on final approval rate and cascade rate by code.
3. Weigh the -40 bps saving against what this window lost (USD 6,354.20 of approved volume).
4. Make the cascade-collapse alert a release gate: it flagged B code 05 daily from 6 Aug, a week before the routing change. Review retryable flags, not only descriptions, in every mapping release.

questions.question: Why did Acquirer B stop recovering 'do not honor' declines through cascading after 6 August 2026?
questions.answer:
**Short answer**
Acquirer B's 'Do not honor' (ISO 05) declines stopped being retried on a second acquirer because change CHG-0806 (decline-code map v2.3 for Acquirer B, 2026-08-06 13:00 UTC) reclassified them from soft/retryable to hard/non-retryable. The change log only says it 'adds R65 handling'; the effect on 05 shows in the data. Hotfix CHG-0815 (v2.3.1, 2026-08-15 13:00 UTC, 'R05 reclassified as soft and retryable') reversed it, and through 2026-08-29 (end of the data) B's 05 declines are retried again.

**What happened**
Window used: 2026-08-06 13:00 to 2026-08-15 13:00 UTC (MX 07:00 to 07:00, CO 08:00 to 08:00 local), from the map change to its hotfix rather than whole calendar days. Segment: payments routed first to B whose first attempt was declined with 05, all cards, MX and CO (B has no 05 rows in BR between 2026-06-01 and 2026-08-29).

| B 05 declines, MX / CO | Retried on another acquirer | Approved on the retry |
|---|---|---|
| Map v2.2, 2026-06-01 to 2026-08-06 | 2,089 of 2,089 / 1,207 of 1,207 | 819 (39.2%) / 418 (34.6%) |
| Map v2.3, 2026-08-06 13:00 to 2026-08-15 13:00 UTC | 0 of 264 / 0 of 314 | 0 / 0 |
| Map v2.3.1, 2026-08-15 13:00 UTC to 2026-08-29 | 438 of 438 / 330 of 330 | 167 / 133 |

Value of the declines that were not retried during v2.3: USD 20,815 (MX) and USD 21,597 (CO).

**Impact**
- Attributable to the missing retries (estimate: non-retried declines x the v2.2 recovery rate, over the window): about 104 approvals and USD 7,967 lost in MX, about 109 approvals and USD 7,597 lost in CO. That is 2.31 pp (MX) and 2.56 pp (CO) of B-routed payments, and 0.42 pp and 0.49 pp of all payments in each country.
- MX country level (fn_drop_impact, vs the prior 14 days): final approval 86.7% to 86.0% (-0.78 pp), 182 fewer approvals than expected, USD 16,263 less approved volume. First-attempt approval was flat (82.9% to 82.8%), so the loss sits in recovery. Acquirer B contributes -0.54 pp (fn_approval_drivers).
- CO country level: before the routing v14 incident (to 2026-08-13 14:00 local) final approval went 86.7% to 86.4% (-0.36 pp, 61 fewer approvals), all of it Acquirer B (-0.37 pp; A +0.01 pp). Over the full window it is 86.7% to 86.0% (-0.77 pp, 161 fewer approvals, USD 4,411), but that includes the routing v14 incident (2026-08-13 19:00 to 2026-08-14 17:10 UTC, INC-0814), which I did not size on its own. In those hours all CO domestic debit went to B, and 148 of the 314 non-retried CO declines fell in them: v14 did not cause the stop (it began on 2026-08-06, before v14), but it concentrated its cost.

**Cause and evidence**
- Platform-side mapping change, not an issuer or acquirer problem. B's 05 was mapped soft/retryable in v2.2, hard/non-retryable in v2.3 and soft/retryable again in v2.3.1, in MX and CO (gold_decline_reasons_daily). fn_cascade_health shows the cascade rate on B's 05 falling from 100% to 0.0% and mapped_as moving from soft to hard (MX full window; CO before v14). The first v2.3 decline was at 13:05 UTC (MX) and 13:13 UTC (CO) on 2026-08-06, right after CHG-0806.
- No surge in declines (fn_decline_shift, same windows): B's 05 declines were 1.2% of payments in the 14-day baseline and 1.1% in the window in MX, 0.9% and 0.9% in CO. B kept returning the same declines; the platform stopped retrying declines the cascade had been recovering (39.2% in MX, 34.6% in CO before the change).
- Scoped to B's 05: A's and C's 05 stayed soft/retryable in all three map versions, and in the same windows B's other codes kept their mapping and cascade rates (1A, 59, 91, 96, TIMEOUT and TECHNICAL_ERROR stayed at 100%). The cascade-collapse alert flagged B/05 in MX and CO every day from 2026-08-06 to 2026-08-14, and no other acquirer/reason pair between 2026-07-15 and 2026-08-29.
- Other changes (fn_changes_near, 240 hours before 2026-08-06 through 2026-08-29, MX, CO and BR): 3DS SDK upgrade 2026-07-28 (before the stop), CO routing v14 and its rollback 2026-08-13/14 (after it started), MX merchant onboarding 2026-08-20 (after the fix). None of them is a decline-mapping change or lines up with the start.

**Recommended actions**
1. Keep v2.3.1 and add a standing check that B's 05 stays soft/retryable with a cascade rate near 100%.
2. Gate every decline-mapping release with an automatic before/after diff of mapped_as and retryable for all codes of the acquirer touched; CHG-0806 named only R65.
3. Send the cascade-collapse alert to the normalization team (owner of both mapping changes) with a same-day response target; this one was flagged every day from 2026-08-06 to 2026-08-14.

questions.question: What happened to approvals in Brazil on the morning of 21 July 2026?
questions.answer:
**What happened**
On 21 July 2026, approvals on Brazil domestic traffic fell sharply between 09:00 and 12:00 BRT (UTC-3), which is 12:00-15:00 UTC, and were back to normal from 12:00. The cause is issuer-side: BR-ISS-03 was largely unavailable during its announced maintenance window, and the retry cascade cannot recover that. I sized the 09:00-12:00 BRT window, not the whole morning or day.

Final approval rate by hour, BR domestic (baseline = same hour, 7-20 July):
- 09:00: 73.4% (94 payments) vs 88.8%
- 10:00: 67.5% (114 payments) vs 88.2%
- 11:00: 75.0% (144 payments) vs 87.0%
- 12:00: 87.3% (166 payments) vs 88.4%
From 06:00 to 08:59 the rate was 89.5%-91.2% (baseline 87.2%-89.7%). Overnight hours have only 6-21 payments each, too few to read, and show no sustained drop.

**Impact** (BR domestic, all card types, 09:00-12:00 BRT vs the previous 14 days)
- Final approval rate 72.2% vs 88.0%: -15.9 pp. First-attempt approval 67.9% vs 84.8%.
- 254 approvals on 352 payments vs about 310 expected at baseline: 56 approvals lost.
- Lost approved volume: USD 4,110.50 (USD 18,348.27 approved out of USD 25,469.10 attempted).

**Cause**
Scheduled maintenance at issuer BR-ISS-03, 12:00-15:00 UTC = 09:00-12:00 BRT (acquirer notice EXT-0721, logged at 08:45 BRT, 15 minutes before the window started).

**Evidence**
- Who moved: BR-ISS-03 (normally 13.8% of BR domestic payments) was approved at only 10.7% (56 payments) vs 88.5% at baseline: -12.4 pp of the -15.9 pp. Other issuers: BR-ISS-02 -1.8 pp, BR-ISS-06 -0.9, BR-ISS-05 -0.8, BR-ISS-07 -0.3, BR-ISS-01 +0.1.
- Both acquirers fell (results are attributed to the first acquirer), which points to a cause common to both: C 87.7% to 74.0% (rate effect -10.6 pp), A 89.3% to 65.8% (-5.3 pp).
- Declines: code 91 'Issuer or switch unavailable' reached 10.2% (C) and 2.6% (A) of all window payments vs 0.3% and 0.1% at baseline (+9.9 and +2.5 pp). No other code rose more than 1.5 pp in the window.
- Retries ran but could not help: code 91 was still retried 100% on both acquirers (as at baseline, still mapped soft, map v2.2), yet recovery fell from 43.4% to 5.6% on C (36 failures) and from 46.4% to 0.0% on A (9 failures).
- Nothing changed on our side: the BR change log from 11 July 00:00 to 22 July 00:00 (BRT) contains only EXT-0721, with no routing, decline-mapping, risk-rule or release change. Routing v13 carried 100% of traffic in both baseline and window. No cascade-collapse alert fired for BR between 14 and 28 July.
- Not a funnel or data issue (all BR traffic): in each hour of the window risk blocks were at most 3.1% and 3DS abandonment at most 1.3% of intents, and no payments had missing acquirer response data in any hour from 00:00 to 14:59.

**Recommended action**
- No rollback and no routing or acquirer change: nothing internal changed, and moving traffic between A and C does not help when the issuer itself is down.
- Tell merchants that BR-ISS-03 cards fail during these windows; hold recurring/subscription retries for those cards until the window ends and offer another payment method.
- Ask the notifying acquirer for earlier notice (this one was logged 15 minutes before the window) and whether more BR-ISS-03 windows are planned.
- Add an hourly, issuer-level alert and show EXT notices on the dashboards. The daily check did not catch this: for the full day of 21 July, BR credit was 88.3% vs 91.0% (28-day baseline) and debit 77.9% vs 81.1% (-2.6 and -3.2 pp), below the anomaly flag.
- Optional: skip the retry of BR-ISS-03 code 91 declines during announced maintenance (retries recovered 5.6% and 0.0%). I did not size the cost of those retries.

**Limits**
- I did not cross-tab decline codes by issuer, so I cannot say how many of the 45 code-91 declines belong to BR-ISS-03. The link rests on its 10.7% approval rate, the matching notice and the code-91 spike.
- About 3.5 pp of the drop (-15.9 total vs -12.4 for BR-ISS-03) is spread over the other issuers and small increases in ordinary declines. The other issuers have only 22-78 payments each in the window, so I cannot attribute it to a specific cause.
- The maintenance is documented only by the acquirer notice in the change log, with no confirmation from the issuer. I did not look at BR-ISS-03 on its own after 12:00; the overall rate was back to normal from the 12:00 hour.

questions.question: Why did conversion in Brazil fall on 18 and 19 June 2026?
questions.answer:
**Why conversion fell in Brazil on 18-19 June**
The risk engine started blocking more payments after Risk rules v3 (a new card-velocity rule, CHG-0618) went live on 18 June at 09:00 Brazil time (12:00 UTC). The loss sits in the risk-block stage, before a payment reaches any acquirer or issuer, so it is neither an acquirer-side nor an issuer-side cause, and a cascade (retry on a second acquirer) cannot recover it. It lasted until the velocity threshold was tuned in v3.1 (CHG-0620) on 20 June at 15:00 Brazil time.

**Window and segment**
18 Jun 09:00 to 20 Jun 15:00, Brazil local time (release to tuning), not the two full calendar days. Brazil, all card types, all traffic. Baseline: the 14 days 4 to 17 June. Conversion = approved / payment intents (includes risk blocks and 3DS abandonment).

**Impact**
- Window: conversion 82.5% vs 85.0% baseline (-2.52 pp); 5,542 intents, 4,573 approved. About 140 fewer approvals than at baseline conversion and about USD 1.9k less approved volume (USD 325k approved in the window).
- Calendar days 18 and 19 June, as you asked: 82.6% vs 85.0% (-2.45 pp), about 121 fewer approvals, about USD 3.5k. By day: 83.5% on 18 June and 81.8% on 19 June, vs a daily range of 84.1% to 86.3% in 4-17 June. These two days include 9 hours before the release (18 Jun 00:00-09:00: conversion 88.1%).
- The USD figures are net of ticket-size mix (so the window figure is lower than the two-day figure); read them as low thousands of USD. The approvals count is the more reliable measure.

**Evidence**
- Risk blocks: 196 of 5,542 intents blocked in the window (3.5%) vs 1.3% at baseline, about 127 more than the baseline rate implies. Daily: 3.0% on 18 June and 4.0% on 19 June vs 0.7% to 1.8% in 4-17 June. Review timeouts did not rise (0.1% vs 0.2% of intents), so these are direct risk blocks.
- Other funnel stages are flat: 3DS abandonment 1.5% vs 1.4%; approval of payments that reached an acquirer 86.9% vs 87.4% (all traffic, same window).
- Timing: before the release (18 Jun 00:00-09:00) risk blocks were 1.6%. Only two changes are logged for Brazil between 8 Jun 00:00 and 21 Jun 00:00 (the check covers routing, risk, release, decline-mapping and partner notices): CHG-0618 (risk rules v3, new card-velocity rule, 18 Jun 09:00) and CHG-0620 (risk rules v3.1, velocity threshold tuned after review, 20 Jun 15:00). On 20 Jun 00:00-15:00 blocks were still 2.9% (conversion 84.0%); from 20 Jun 15:00 to 21 Jun 23:59 they were 1.1% and conversion 85.4%, back to baseline.
- Broad-based (18-19 Jun vs 4-17 Jun): credit 3.5% vs 1.3%, debit 3.6% vs 1.2%, web 3.5% vs 1.3%, app 3.6% vs 1.2%.

**Acquirer side checked**
For payments that reached an acquirer (same window and 14-day baseline): final approval 87.6% vs 88.0% (-0.33 pp, 16 fewer approvals), all on routing v12 in both periods, so no routing change. The small dip is spread out (largest: issuer BR-ISS-01 -0.48 pp, acquirer C -0.23 pp). questions.question: Which acquirer had the higher final approval rate on domestic credit cards in Mexico in July 2026, A or C, and by how much?
questions.answer:
**A had the higher final approval rate, by about 0.7 percentage points (0.65 pp before rounding).**

Segment and period: Mexico, domestic credit cards (not cross-border), 1 to 31 July 2026 (local dates). Final approval rate = final approved / payments sent to an acquirer, attributed to the first acquirer chosen by routing.

| Acquirer | Payments sent | Final approved | Final approval rate | First-attempt approval rate |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | 27,501 | 24,549 | 89.3% | 86.2% |
| C | 18,301 | 16,217 | 88.6% | 85.5% |

What to keep in mind:
- The lead is small. The 95% margin of error on the gap is about +/-0.59 pp (simple binomial approximation), so A's 0.65 pp lead only just clears sampling noise.
- It is not one bad day. A was ahead on 21 of the 31 days, C on 9, and the two were level on 30 July (88.6% each). Daily final rates stayed between 87.3% and 91.4% for A and between 86.1% and 91.4% for C. I did not look at hourly data.
- Final rates credit the first acquirer, so they include approvals recovered by a cascade retry on another acquirer (832 for A, 569 for C). On first attempt alone the order is the same: A 86.2% vs C 85.5%.
- The counts match the payment-level data (silver_payments) exactly for both acquirers, with no payments flagged as missing attempt data.
- I did not investigate why A is ahead (no checks on drivers, issuer or routing-rule mix, decline codes, cascade health or production changes), so I am not naming a cause.

questions.question: Compare the first-attempt approval of Acquirers A and B on domestic debit cards in Mexico in July 2026.
questions.answer:
**In July 2026, on domestic debit cards in Mexico, Acquirer A had the higher first-attempt approval: 79.8% vs 76.3% for Acquirer B (A ahead by 3.4 pp).**

Segment and period: Mexico, debit, domestic only (is_cross_border = false), 1 to 31 July 2026 (local dates). Payments are attributed to the first acquirer chosen by routing. First-attempt approval = approved on the first attempt / payments sent (payments that reached an acquirer), with no cascade retries counted.

| Acquirer | Payments sent | Approved on first attempt | First-attempt approval | Soft declines | Hard declines | Technical failures |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | 15,130 | 12,072 | 79.8% | 15.6% | 3.7% | 0.9% |
| B | 15,148 | 11,564 | 76.3% | 17.5% | 4.7% | 1.4% |

Decline columns are the share of payments sent that failed on the first attempt for that reason; all percentages are rounded. B is higher on all three failure types, with the largest difference in soft declines (17.5% vs 15.6%).

**How solid the gap is**
- Size: 3.4 pp on unrounded rates, with a 95% confidence interval of 2.5 to 4.4 pp, so it is outside sampling noise.
- Consistency: A was ahead on 29 of the 31 days. B was ahead only on 2 July (by 0.7 pp) and 8 July (by 0.3 pp). The gap was widest at the end of the month: 7.8 pp on 29 July and 10.4 pp on 31 July (A 82.7% vs B 72.3%).
- Traffic mix does not explain it, on the dimensions I checked: A and B received a very similar mix by issuer, card brand, merchant segment and 3DS authentication, and A was ahead in all 8 issuers, in Visa (79.5% vs 76.8%) and Mastercard (80.2% vs 75.6%), in all 7 named merchant segments, with and without 3DS authentication, and under both routing rule versions seen in July (v13, about 95% of each acquirer's payments: 79.7% vs 76.4%; v12, about 5%: 81.4% vs 75.5%).
- Data quality: for MX domestic debit payments routed first to A or B on 1 to 31 July 2026, every payment reached an acquirer and none had missing acquirer-response data. The monthly totals in the daily summary table match the payment-level data.

**Context**
- Final approval (first attempt plus cascade retries, attributed to the first acquirer): A 83.7% vs B 81.9%. Retries recovered 840 payments for B and 596 for A, which is why the gap is smaller after the cascade.
- The MX change log from 21 June to 31 July 2026 (local time) lists two changes: CHG-0702 on 2 July, 09:00, 'Routing v13: 10% of MX debit to Acquirer C (A/B test)', and CHG-0728 on 28 July, 10:00, '3DS SDK upgrade on web checkout' (MX and CO). Acquirer C is not part of this comparison.

**What I did not check**
These are descriptive numbers. I did not run the cause analysis (approval drivers, decline-code shift, cascade health, or the effect of the two logged changes), so I cannot say why B's first-attempt approval is lower than A's. If you want, I can break B's extra declines down by reason code on domestic debit, or look at the last days of July.

questions.question: Was there any early warning before the Colombia debit incident of 13 August 2026?
questions.answer:
**Short answer:** Yes, one. It was in cascade health, not in the CO debit approval rate. Acquirer B stopped retrying code 05 ('Do not honor') declines on 6 Aug, and the cascade alert table flagged it every day for the 7 days before the incident (6 to 12 Aug). CO debit approval looked normal because debit only reached Acquirer B when routing v14 went live on 13 Aug at 14:00 (all times Bogota).

**The warning**
- `gold_cascade_alerts_daily`, Acquirer B, reason 05: is_alert = true every day from 6 to 12 Aug in CO (14 to 27 failures a day on 7 to 12 Aug) and also in MX. Cascade rate 0.0% (5.0% on 6 Aug) against a healthy baseline of 100.0%. These are the only alert rows in the whole table, in any country (data covers 1 Jun to 29 Aug).
- Trigger: CHG-0806, 6 Aug 08:00, decline-code mapping v2.3 for Acquirer B, described only as 'adds R65 handling'. The text does not mention code 05, but the data shows B/05 switching from soft and retryable to hard and non-retryable that day (CO, all card types):

| Period | Map version | B/05 class | Failures per day | Retried | Recovered per day |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 30 Jul - 5 Aug | v2.2 | soft, retryable | 8 to 28 | all | 5 to 15 |
| 6 Aug | v2.2, then v2.3 | 1 soft, 19 hard | 20 | 1 | 0 |
| 7 - 12 Aug | v2.3 | hard, not retryable | 14 to 27 | 0 | 0 |
| 13 and 14 Aug | v2.3 | hard, not retryable | 109 and 60 (debit 93 and 44) | 0 | 0 |
| 16 - 20 Aug | v2.3.1 | soft, retryable | 16 to 27 | all | 5 to 15 |

On 15 Aug, 2 failures were still under v2.3 (not retried) and 18 under v2.3.1 (all retried, 8 recovered). No alerts after 14 Aug (checked to 29 Aug).

- Why debit did not show it: CO domestic debit went only to Acquirer A until 13 Aug 14:00 (daily data from 14 Jul to 12 Aug show no other first acquirer), and B/05 had zero debit failures every day from 30 Jul to 12 Aug. The CO alerts of 6 to 12 Aug were all on credit cards. The alert table has no card-type split.

**Where I found no warning (period checked)**
- Anomaly table, CO debit domestic, 14 Jul to 12 Aug: no day flagged. Worst was -1.9 pp on 9 Aug (84.8% vs 86.7% baseline).
- Driver check, 6 Aug to 13 Aug 00:00 vs the 14 days before, CO debit: no segment moved the rate by more than 0.4 pp.
- Acquirer A, 14 Jul to 12 Aug: daily final approval 84.8% to 88.6%, technical failures at most 1.4% of payments, p95 latency 1,155 to 1,298 ms.
- Change log for CO, 1 Jun to 15 Aug 00:00: five entries (checkout UI release 3 Jun, 3DS SDK upgrade 28 Jul, CHG-0806, the routing change and its rollback). No external partner notice, and no corrective change between 6 Aug and 13 Aug.

**The incident** (window used: 13 Aug 14:00 to 14 Aug 12:10, routing v14 to its rollback, not the whole day)
- CHG-0813 sent 100% of CO domestic debit to B (cost optimization, -40 bps). CHG-0814 rolled back to v13 (INC-0814).
- Impact, CO debit vs the 14 days before the window: final approval 75.6% vs 86.5% (-10.95 pp), first attempt 70.7% vs 84.6%. About 110 approvals lost (759 vs 869 expected) and USD 6,354 of approved volume (USD 47,096 approved of USD 61,689 attempted).
- Cause (checked): acquirer B and routing v14 carry the whole -10.95 pp, and the three issuers with the largest effect all fell together (CO-ISS-01 80.0% vs 87.8%, CO-ISS-02 74.6% vs 87.9%, CO-ISS-03 72.4% vs 84.8%), so it is not issuer-specific. On B, 05 failed 137 of the 1,004 payments, mapped hard, 0.0% retried and 0.0% recovered (v2.3). On A in the baseline, 05 was mapped soft and retried 98.4% of the time. Retrying this code did recover payments before the change (table above), so this is a cascade-recoverable cause, not an issuer-side one.
- How fast it showed: hourly final approval was 73.2% at 14:00 and 67.2% at 15:00 on 13 Aug, vs 83.0% to 88.6% in every hour from 07:00 to 13:00 that day. The daily detector flagged 13 Aug (79.4% vs 86.7% baseline, -7.33 pp) but not 14 Aug (84.6%, -1.85 pp).

**Recommended actions**
1. Give cascade alerts an owner and an escalation path, like approval anomalies: B/05 alerted for 7 days with no corrective change in the CO log.
2. Before a routing change moves traffic to an acquirer, check that acquirer's open cascade alerts: B/05 was alerting when v14 shipped.
3. Add an hourly approval check with a rollback trigger for the first hours after a routing change.
4. Regression-test every mapping change for the retry class of the main codes (05, 51, 1A): the CHG-0806 text did not list the 05 effect. Confirm with the owners that v2.3.1 is the intended permanent fix.

**Not checked**
- I cannot split the -10.95 pp between B's lower first-attempt approval and the missing 05 retry.
- Losses on CO credit and MX during 6 to 14 Aug were not sized.
- Codes 51 and 65 on B are mapped soft but show 0.0% retried in the window. I have no A baseline for them here, so I did not treat them as part of the cause.
- I did not retrieve the change-log entry for v2.3.1 (my change search ended 15 Aug 00:00).

questions.question: Which Colombian issuer had the lowest final approval on domestic debit cards during the incident window, from 13 August 2026 14:00 to 14 August 2026 12:10 local time?
questions.answer:
**CO-ISS-07 had the lowest final approval on domestic debit cards in your window: 65.3% (47 approved of 72 payments sent).**

Segment and period: Colombia, domestic debit cards (is_cross_border = false). Final approval = final_approved / payments_sent, so cascade recoveries are included. Window: 13 Aug 2026 14:00 to 14 Aug 2026 12:10, Colombia local time (UTC-5), start included, end excluded. I used payment-level data because the hourly and daily tables cannot cut at 12:10. For the whole hours inside the window it matches gold_approval_hourly exactly (746 approved of 987 sent, 75.6%, for the whole segment).

| Issuer | Payments sent | Final approved | Final approval in window | Same issuer, prior 14 days |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CO-ISS-07 | 72 | 47 | 65.3% | 84.9% |
| CO-ISS-03 | 145 | 105 | 72.4% | 84.8% |
| CO-ISS-05 | 96 | 70 | 72.9% | 84.6% |
| CO-ISS-02 | 169 | 126 | 74.6% | 87.9% |
| CO-ISS-04 | 110 | 84 | 76.4% | 86.0% |
| CO-ISS-06 | 118 | 91 | 77.1% | 87.0% |
| CO-ISS-01 | 230 | 184 | 80.0% | 87.8% |
| CO-ISS-08 | 64 | 52 | 81.3% | 87.0% |

Prior 14 days = 30 Jul 14:00 to 13 Aug 14:00 Colombia time, the same baseline fn_approval_drivers uses.

How to read it:
- Treat the exact order with care. CO-ISS-07 had only 72 payments in the window, so its rate carries a wide margin of error. CO-ISS-03 (72.4%) and CO-ISS-05 (72.9%) are close behind on more volume, so the order of the bottom three is indicative, not firm.
- The lowest rate is not the main driver of the drop. CO-ISS-07 normally runs at 84.9%, in line with the other issuers' prior-14-day rates (84.6% to 87.9%), and it has the largest fall against its own baseline, so it is not simply an issuer that is always weak. But all eight issuers were below their own baseline. fn_approval_drivers puts domestic Colombian debit 10.95 pp below its prior-14-day baseline in this window. The largest contributions come from CO-ISS-02 (-2.25 pp), CO-ISS-03 (-1.8 pp) and CO-ISS-01 (-1.8 pp), while CO-ISS-07 contributes -1.41 pp because it carries 7.2% of the window's payments.
- Change log. fn_changes_near for Colombia (3 Aug 14:00 to 14 Aug 12:10) lists two changes: CHG-0806 (6 Aug 08:00, decline-code mapping v2.3 for Acquirer B) and CHG-0813 (13 Aug 14:00, routing v14 sends 100% of CO domestic debit to Acquirer B). The window starts at the same minute as CHG-0813. Nothing else affecting Colombia is listed in that range, so I cannot tie the 12:10 end to a logged change.

Not checked: I did not run the decline-code shift or cascade-health checks, and I did not look at the acquirer or routing-version split, so I am not attributing a cause to the drop, to CHG-0813 or to CHG-0806. I can run those next if you want the why.
